posts.title: Mini-story: Debrief
posts.description: The last normal thing Heller saw was the elderly lady who lived a few doors down, heading out on her usual Friday-morning trip to the supermarket. She was a pleasant old dear — he thought her name was Margaret, or Mary, or something like that — and she always said hello to him, or at least waved. posts.title: Mini-story: Overalls
posts.description: It was hot as hell. Hot enough that Carr only had to roll the sleeves of his overalls twice and they stayed at his elbows. Hot enough that the dirty city fleetingly seemed exotic, or at least grimy in a foreign, accented sort of way. He felt a droplet of sweat running down his back, and he ignored it. There probably wasn’t that much longer to wait anyway. Discomfort, like pain, was an experience.

posts.title: Mini-story: The True Death
posts.description: In our society, there are two deaths. In the past, in less enlightened times, we considered only the physical process of dying. The end of a life, where we ritually gathered — as we still do — to take stock of someone’s existence. But those ceremonies lack their central participant, who is already gone.
